draft.title: Naming the sides of a right-angled triangle
card: Hypotenuse
The longest side. It is always opposite the right angle, and it does not change when you pick a different angle.
Opposite
The side across from the angle you are using. It does not touch that angle.
Adjacent
The side next to the angle you are using that is not the hypotenuse. Adjacent means next to.
Opposite and adjacent depend on the angle chosen. In a triangle ABC with the right angle at C, the side BC is opposite angle \(A\). If you use angle \(B\) instead, BC becomes the adjacent side.
draft.remember: The hypotenuse faces the right angle. Opposite and adjacent are named from the angle you use.

a.q: In a right-angled triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
opts: The side opposite the right angle
The side opposite the chosen angle
The side next to the chosen angle
The shortest side of the triangle
a.why: The hypotenuse is always across from the right angle, and it is the longest side. The side opposite the chosen angle is the opposite side, and that changes when you pick a different angle.
a.clue: Which side faces the right angle?

b.q: In triangle PQR, the right angle is at Q. PQ is 5 cm, QR is 12 cm and PR is 13 cm. Using angle \(R\), which side is adjacent?
opts: Side QR
Side PQ
Side PR
Both PQ and PR
b.why: The adjacent side touches angle \(R\) and is not the hypotenuse. PR touches \(R\) but is the hypotenuse, since it faces the right angle at Q. PQ is the opposite side, as it does not touch \(R\).
b.clue: Find the hypotenuse first, then see which other side touches angle R.

wants.brief: A right-angled triangle ABC with the right angle at C marked by a small square. C is at the bottom left, A at the bottom right and B directly above C. Angle A is marked with an arc. Label side AB as hypotenuse, side BC as opposite angle A, and side AC as adjacent to angle A. Place each label beside its own side, clear of the vertex letters.
wants.why: Seeing the three sides named from angle A shows how the names depend on the chosen angle.

a.best: The side opposite the right angle

problems.detail: The clue 'Which side faces the right angle?' restates the right option almost word for word, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts, answers and explanations are correct: the hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, and QR is adjacent to R in triangle PQR. The only issue is that the clue for question a practically gives the answer away.
